If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism drift.  
When sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in consecutive days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction to forecast at 15–30 day horizon to dampen volatility overreaction.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.4% per day for late horizon (21–30 days) to prevent momentum overestimation.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope by 0.2–0.4% per day for late horizon to offset bearish sentiment lag.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast at 1–5 day horizon to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
